details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:585-626 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: --list-violated-files can add out-of-tree fingerprint paths to the violated set and print them to stdout.
  WHY: Reviewers consistently traced this to unsatisfied fingerprints with rejected paths being emitted as resolver allowlist entries, which breaks the stdout contract and can expose unsafe filesystem paths outside the checkout.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:506-556 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: capture_baseline_state opens the baseline file without creating parent directories first.
  WHY: Nested --baseline-fingerprints-state paths raise FileNotFoundError, fall into the warn-only handler, and leave compare mode without a baseline.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:730-842 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: Legacy verify() still counts invalid must_contain regexes in the denominator before rejecting compile errors.
  WHY: This can spuriously trigger the silent-regression detector with an inflated satisfaction ratio; x-ai_grok-4_20 noted compare mode was fixed but the default legacy path still has the bug.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:666-677 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: PRE_EXISTING_FINGERPRINT_DRIFT_V1 markers are emitted in a JSON-embedded fp_key format instead of the documented structured key=value fields.
  WHY: Downstream drift-audit tooling has to JSON-parse each marker rather than consuming explicit fields, which reviewers flagged as contract drift and more error-prone.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:698-709 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: compare-mode PASSED output does not include the pre_existing_drift_count/newly_fixed summary counts.
  WHY: Operators must grep individual drift markers to determine magnitude instead of seeing a summary line.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:826 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: The mutually-exclusive-arguments error message includes a trailing period that does not match the documented exact string.
  WHY: Exact-string log greps and contract tests can miss the error.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:438-470 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The new content_unavailable path in _violation_message only affects must_contain; the must_not_contain + content_unavailable case never reaches it because _fp_satisfied treats missing content as satisfied.
  WHY: Reviewers agreed this is currently dead/unreachable code and, if the semantics ever change, the diagnostic would be incomplete.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:102-148 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: _resolve_repo_path anchors validation to os.getcwd() with realpath/commonpath, so path validation can misbehave when the verifier is launched from a subdirectory or through symlinked paths.
  WHY: Reviewers described both false rejection of legitimate repo-relative paths and a potential boundary weakness if cwd or symlink targets are manipulated; the concern was disputed by deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, which said the symlink-bypass claim was incorrect.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:133-148 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: _read_file only handles FileNotFoundError, so directory paths raise IsADirectoryError and crash the verifier.
  WHY: A fingerprint path of "." or another directory would produce a traceback instead of a handled violation/warning.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:666-788 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: compare-mode PASSED messages append a branch suffix, changing the exact output contract from the legacy verify message.
  WHY: Reviewers flagged downstream log parsers and contract tests as sensitive to the exact PASSED string.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:730-743 | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The legacy verify() function still increments mc_total_expected before rejecting uncompilable must_contain regexes.
  WHY: This inflates the silent-regression denominator and can warn with a misleading ratio even when all valid patterns are satisfied.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:607-611 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: list_violated_files can add out-of-tree fingerprint paths to the violated set and print them to stdout.
  WHY: Downstream resolver allowlists may receive filesystem paths outside the checkout, breaking the stdout contract.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:550-553 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: capture_baseline_state writes the baseline file without creating parent directories first.
  WHY: Nested --baseline-fingerprints-state paths raise FileNotFoundError, trigger the warn-only handler, and leave compare mode without a baseline.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:595-615 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The function adds out-of-tree fingerprint paths to the violated set and prints them to stdout.
  WHY: When _fp_satisfied returns False for must_contain because content is None, the path gets emitted via --list-violated-files and can be passed downstream as an unsafe allowlist entry.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:506-555 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: capture_baseline_state writes the baseline file directly without first creating parent directories.
  WHY: A nested baseline path like some/missing/dir/baseline.json fails, falls into the warning handler, and silently leaves compare mode without a baseline.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:666-674 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The marker format uses issue={issue_num} and fp_key={_fp_key_json(fp_key)} instead of the documented explicit fields.
  WHY: Downstream drift-audit tooling must JSON-parse each marker rather than consuming plain key=value fields.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:698-708 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: When pre_existing_drift or newly_fixed is nonzero, the PASSED message does not include count summaries.
  WHY: Operators have to grep PRE_EXISTING_FINGERPRINT_DRIFT_V1 markers to determine drift magnitude.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:826 | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The mutual-exclusion error message ends with a trailing period.
  WHY: Automation expecting the documented exact string will fail to match it.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:438-470 | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The content_unavailable handling is effectively only used for must_contain; the must_not_contain case is unreachable.
  WHY: This is dead code today, and the explicit unavailable-path diagnostic never appears for must_not_contain patterns.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM mistralai_mistral-small-2603 ===
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:_resolve_repo_path function (introduced in last_run_diff) | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: _resolve_repo_path uses os.path.realpath and os.path.commonpath but still allows path-validation ambiguity around symlinks and repository anchoring.
  WHY: The reviewer concluded an attacker-controlled fingerprint path could craft a symlink-based traversal that violates the repository sandbox boundary.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:list_violated_files function (lines ~600-626) | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Out-of-tree absolute paths from fingerprints are considered unsatisfied, added to stdout's violated set, and printed as resolver allowlist entries.
  WHY: This violates the --list-violated-files stdout contract by emitting filesystem paths outside the repository root.
=== END FINDINGS FROM mistralai_mistral-small-2603 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:585-615 | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The function adds raw fingerprint paths to the violated set and prints them to stdout in --list-violated-files mode without filtering out-of-tree paths.
  WHY: Downstream consumers of --list-violated-files stdout may receive absolute paths outside the repository root and attempt to operate on them.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:506-556 | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The function opens out_path for writing without first ensuring parent directories exist.
  WHY: A nested --baseline-fingerprints-state path fails with FileNotFoundError, is only warned about, and compare mode silently falls back to absolute verification.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:666-677 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The drift markers use fp_key={_fp_key_json(fp_key)} which embeds the file path and regex as a JSON list.
  WHY: Drift-audit tooling must JSON-parse each marker instead of consuming plain key=value fields, making downstream automation more complex and error-prone.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:698-709 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: When pre_existing_drift > 0 or newly_fixed > 0, compare mode does not emit drift summary counts.
  WHY: Operators cannot quickly assess drift magnitude without grepping all PRE_EXISTING_FINGERPRINT_DRIFT_V1 markers.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:826 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The mutual-exclusion error message ends with a trailing period.
  WHY: The documented exact string used for log-grepping and contract tests omits the period.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:_violation_message() at lines 444-456 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The must_not_contain + content_unavailable path is absent because _fp_satisfied returns satisfied=True when content is missing.
  WHY: The code structure suggests handling for that case, but it never executes and would lose precision if the semantics ever changed.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:compare_against_baseline() and main() PASSED messages | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Compare-mode PASSED lines append (branch=...) via _branch_suffix(branch), changing the byte-compatible output contract.
  WHY: Downstream log parsers and contract tests keyed on the exact PASSED string can fail to recognize successful compare-mode runs.
=== END FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_6-plus ===
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:_resolve_repo_path (lines ~120-132 in last_run_diff, also used in _read_file ~133-148) | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The out-of-tree path guard uses os.path.realpath(os.getcwd()) as the repo-root anchor, so invoking from a subdirectory can make valid repo-relative paths look outside the repository.
  WHY: Legitimate relative paths can be rejected with "fingerprint path resolves outside repository root" warnings and cause false-violation reporting.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:_resolve_repo_path (lines ~120-132) | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The repo-root anchor is derived from os.getcwd() and compared with realpath/commonpath, so the anchor can drift if the cwd assumption is wrong or changes between checks.
  WHY: This is a defense-in-depth gap that can silently shrink the security boundary to a subdirectory instead of the full repository.
